title: Introducing GPT-5.5
gist: OpenAI launches GPT-5.5 as a step up in agentic coding, computer use, knowledge work and science, claiming state-of-the-art on Terminal-Bench 2.0 (82.7%) and GDPval (84.9%) at GPT-5.4 latency with fewer tokens, priced at $5/$30 per 1M tokens, with High cyber and bio classification and expanded Trusted Access for Cyber.

insights.claim: GPT-5.5 scores 82.7% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 versus 75.1% for GPT-5.4, 69.4% for Claude Opus 4.7 and 68.5% for Gemini 3.1 Pro, and 73.1% on OpenAI's internal Expert-SWE versus 68.5%.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Leads on agentic command-line coding; track competitive benchmark leadership among OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.

insights.claim: On SWE-Bench Pro GPT-5.5 reaches 58.6%, below Claude Opus 4.7's 64.3%, and OpenAI notes labs have seen evidence of memorization on that eval.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: The lead is not uniform; Anthropic still tops this real-world GitHub issue benchmark.
insights.quote: Labs have noted evidence of memorization

insights.claim: GPT-5.5 scores 84.9% on GDPval (wins or ties across 44 occupations), 78.7% on OSWorld-Verified, 98.0% on Tau2-bench Telecom, 60.0% on FinanceAgent and 88.5% on internal investment-banking modeling tasks.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Knowledge-work automation benchmarks are approaching high levels, supporting white-collar task-substitution theses, including finance.

insights.claim: Long-context performance improves sharply: OpenAI MRCR v2 8-needle at 512K-1M rises to 74.0% from 36.6% for GPT-5.4, and Graphwalks BFS at 1M tokens to 45.4% from 9.4%.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Usable 1M-token context enables larger codebase and document workloads.

insights.claim: GPT-5.5 scores 85.0% on ARC-AGI-2 (Verified) versus 73.3% for GPT-5.4, 75.8% for Opus 4.7 and 77.1% for Gemini 3.1 Pro, and 35.4% on FrontierMath Tier 4 versus 27.1%.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Abstract-reasoning and hard-math gains are large generation-over-generation.

insights.claim: GPT-5.5 matches GPT-5.4 per-token latency while using significantly fewer tokens on Codex tasks, and on Artificial Analysis's Coding Index OpenAI claims state-of-the-art at half the cost of competitive frontier coding models.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Capability per dollar is improving, pressuring competitors' pricing and per-task inference margins.

insights.claim: API pricing for gpt-5.5 is $5 per 1M input and $30 per 1M output tokens with a 1M context window, and gpt-5.5-pro is $30 and $180; Batch and Flex are half price and Priority is 2.5x.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Pricing is above GPT-5.4; OpenAI bets token efficiency offsets it. Reference for inference revenue modelling.

insights.claim: Codex Fast mode generates tokens 1.5x faster at 2.5x the cost, and Codex offers GPT-5.5 with a 400K context window.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog

insights.claim: GPT-5.5 was co-designed for, trained with, and served on NVIDIA GB200 and GB300 NVL72 systems, and Codex-written load-balancing heuristics raised token generation speed by over 20%.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: NVIDIA rack-scale systems remain the reference platform for OpenAI's frontier serving; models are improving their own serving stack.
insights.quote: the model helped improve the infrastructure that serves it

insights.claim: More than 85% of OpenAI uses Codex weekly across engineering, finance, communications, marketing, data science and product, and its finance team used it to review 24,771 K-1 forms (71,637 pages), finishing two weeks faster than the prior year.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Internal dogfooding evidence for non-engineering agent adoption in the enterprise.

insights.claim: An internal GPT-5.5 with a custom harness helped discover a new proof about off-diagonal Ramsey numbers, later verified in Lean, and OpenAI calls the model a 'bona fide co-scientist' for biomedical research.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Frontier models are beginning to produce original mathematical results, boosting the science-acceleration narrative.

insights.claim: GeneBench scores 25.0% for GPT-5.5 versus 19.0% for GPT-5.4 (33.2% for GPT-5.5 Pro), and BixBench 80.5% versus 74.0%.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Genetics and bioinformatics analysis is improving but absolute GeneBench scores remain low.

insights.claim: OpenAI classifies GPT-5.5's biological/chemical and cybersecurity capabilities as High under its Preparedness Framework, a step up from GPT-5.4 but not Critical on cyber.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Capability thresholds are being approached; regulatory and safeguard costs rise with each tier.

insights.claim: OpenAI is deploying stricter cyber classifiers and, via Trusted Access for Cyber, offering fewer-restriction cyber-permissive models to verified defenders, including critical-infrastructure organisations.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Gated, authenticated access to dual-use cyber capability is becoming the industry template; opens a market for AI-driven defense.

insights.claim: GPT-5.5 reached ChatGPT and Codex first and the API later because API deployments need different safeguards, with API rollout following within a day.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: API availability is gated on safeguards for scaled serving.
